findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:~70 — The script body treats `span-buf:s:*` keys as sorted sets (`zcard`/`zunionstore`/`zpopmin`) and buffer.py writes them via `zadd`, but the unchanged tail of the script still inserts the incoming span payload with `sadd` into the same `set_key`/`span_key`; `sadd` on a zset (or `zcard`/`zunionstore` on a key the tail created as a set) raises WRONGTYPE, so the script errors on live data — the payload insertion must also be converted to `zadd` with the timestamp as score.

[Critical/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:~72 — `organization_context` is never defined in `get()` (no such variable exists in this endpoint) but is dereferenced unconditionally on every request to compute `enable_advanced`, so every GET raises NameError and the audit-log endpoint returns 500 for all users.

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py (OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, negative-offset branch) — Slices the queryset with a negative start offset; Django ORM querysets raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` (the comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing automatically is false), so the 'advanced' path crashes whenever a negative-offset cursor is used.

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py (OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key) — Copies OffsetPaginator's `int(math.floor/ceil(value))` key handling, but the audit-log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"` where the key attribute is a `datetime` object; `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError on any request that returns rows (this conversion is exactly why DateTimePaginator exists).

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:~82 — `self.paginate(..., enable_advanced_features=True)` passes a keyword that `paginate()` does not accept (paginator constructor options are passed via `paginator_options=`), raising TypeError; the flag never reaches the paginator.

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~179 (OffsetPaginator.get_result) — The change to the shared default paginator silently alters behavior for negative cursor offsets (which clients can craft): forward cursors are clamped to offset 0 and return the first page as silently wrong results instead of erroring, while prev cursors still pass negative offsets straight to the queryset and crash; this affects every endpoint using the default paginator with no actual performance benefit.

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py (OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result) — `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:` compares a slice length (at most `limit + extra`) against `offset + limit + extra`, so it can only be true when offset == 0; for prev cursors with a non-zero offset the boundary row is never trimmed (the base class compares against the fetched length), producing an extra/overlapping row in prev pages.

[Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:~62 — `zpopmin` eviction permanently drops the oldest spans from a segment before it is flushed, with no metric or log emitted (the removed `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric was the only signal for this condition), so segments flush silently incomplete and the data loss is undetectable.

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/ — No test exercises the new eviction path (`span_count > 1000` → `zpopmin`), and every test span uses the identical `end_timestamp_precise` (1700000000.0), so score-based zset ordering and eviction-by-age behavior are completely untested.

[Medium/test_gap] There are no tests for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` or the `optimized_pagination` endpoint branch; even a basic test would have immediately caught the NameError, the invalid `paginate()` kwarg, and the negative-slicing/datetime crashes.

[Low/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Redirect loop bound cut from 10000 to 1000 and the comment documenting the depth limit deleted; chains deeper than 1000 now exit mid-chain and the following `hset` records a redirect to an intermediate span, splitting deep trees into multiple segments — the exact failure the removed comment warned about.

[Low/bug] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:~449 — The eviction cap is hardcoded to 1000 in the Lua script while the flush-side `max_segment_spans` enforcement (and its metric) was removed from `_load_segment_data`; the two limits are now disconnected, so deployments configuring `max_segment_spans` below 1000 get no enforcement at all.

[Low/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:~140 — `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is read with no fallback; a message produced before this field was added to the schema (or with a null value) raises KeyError and fails the entire consumer batch (and `None` would also be rejected as a `zadd` score); should use `.get()` with a fallback such as `val["timestamp"]`.

[Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~819 — `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is documented as an 'Enhanced cursor-based paginator,' but it is a copy of the offset-based `OffsetPaginator` (pages by `cursor.offset` slicing, never by cursor value); the added cursors.py comment likewise claims negative offsets are 'allowed' when nothing supports them — the docs describe behavior the code does not have.

[Low/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:~70 — New undocumented `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter makes the same endpoint use a different paginator with different edge-case semantics depending on the caller's privileges (superuser/global-access vs. everyone else), an invisible, unversioned API behavior change that is also unrelated to this PR's stated purpose (spans buffer).

However, the diff does not include the implementation or signature of `paginate()` (likely on `ControlSiloOrganizationEndpoint`/base endpoint), so we cannot verify from this diff whether `paginate()` rejects unknown kwargs (raising `TypeError`) or forwards them to the paginator (e.g., via `paginator_options` or `**kwargs`). The claim that `paginate()` “does not accept” this keyword and that it must be passed via `paginator_options` is therefore not verifiable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py (OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result) — `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:` compares a slice length (at most `limit + extra`) against `offset + limit + extra`, so it can only be true when offset == 0; for prev cursors with a non-zero offset the boundary row is never trimmed (the base class compares against the fetched length), producing an extra/overlapping row in prev pages.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:` check is inconsistent with how `results` is sliced just above. `results` is built from `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `stop = start_offset + limit + extra`, so the maximum possible `len(results)` is `limit + extra` (i.e., `stop - start_offset`). Comparing that to `offset + limit + extra` will generally never be true when `offset != 0` (and for negative offsets the relationship is also inconsistent), so the intended trimming path for prev-cursor boundary handling will often be skipped, risking extra/overlapping rows on prev pages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:~62 — `zpopmin` eviction permanently drops the oldest spans from a segment before it is flushed, with no metric or log emitted (the removed `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric was the only signal for this condition), so segments flush silently incomplete and the data loss is undetectable.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds an explicit cap in `add-buffer.lua`:
- It computes `span_count` and if `span_count > 1000` it calls `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)`, which permanently removes the oldest entries from the segment ZSET.
- There is no metric/log emitted around this eviction in the Lua script.
In parallel, the diff removes the prior detection path in `spans/buffer.py` that used to enforce `max_segment_spans` and emit `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded")` plus an error log when too many spans were present; that entire span-count guard block is deleted and replaced with unconditional `payloads[key].extend(...)`.
Together, the change makes truncation/data loss possible and (per the diff) silent/undetectable, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/ — No test exercises the new eviction path (`span_count > 1000` → `zpopmin`), and every test span uses the identical `end_timestamp_precise` (1700000000.0), so score-based zset ordering and eviction-by-age behavior are completely untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial eviction/ordering behavior in `add-buffer.lua`: it tracks `span_count` and, when `span_count > 1000`, evicts via `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)`. In the updated tests, the changes shown only add `end_timestamp_precise` fields (e.g. `1700000000.0` in `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` and `test_consumer.py`, and `now` reused for all spans in `test_flusher.py`) and do not add any scenario that would create >1000 spans in a set to hit the `zpopmin` eviction path. Also, using identical `end_timestamp_precise` values means the zset score-based ordering (and thus age-based eviction semantics) isn’t meaningfully exercised by these tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] There are no tests for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` or the `optimized_pagination` endpoint branch; even a basic test would have immediately caught the NameError, the invalid `paginate()` kwarg, and the negative-slicing/datetime crashes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior (new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` in `sentry/api/paginator.py` and a new `optimized_pagination` GET-controlled branch in `organization_auditlogs.py`), but no tests are added/updated to exercise either path. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded test gap. However, the finding’s specific claims about a guaranteed `NameError`, an invalid `paginate()` kwarg, and datetime crashes are not directly verifiable from the shown diff (e.g., we can’t see `paginate()`’s signature or the module imports), so only the “missing tests for the new branch/class” portion is strongly supported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Redirect loop bound cut from 10000 to 1000 and the comment documenting the depth limit deleted; chains deeper than 1000 now exit mid-chain and the following `hset` records a redirect to an intermediate span, splitting deep trees into multiple segments — the exact failure the removed comment warned about.

adjudication.rationale: In `add-buffer.lua`, the redirect-walk loop bound is reduced from `for i = 0, 10000 do  -- ...` to `for i = 0, 1000 do` and the loop has no fallback/error when the bound is hit. If the redirect chain is longer than 1000, the loop will terminate due to the `for` bound rather than reaching a terminal `new_set_span == set_span_id`/nil, leaving `set_span_id` at an intermediate node. The subsequent `redis.call("hset", main_redirect_key, span_id, set_span_id)` will then record a redirect to that intermediate span, which can split what would otherwise be a single joined chain/tree into multiple segments. This is a behavior change that can break correctness for deep chains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:~449 — The eviction cap is hardcoded to 1000 in the Lua script while the flush-side `max_segment_spans` enforcement (and its metric) was removed from `_load_segment_data`; the two limits are now disconnected, so deployments configuring `max_segment_spans` below 1000 get no enforcement at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the flush-side `max_segment_spans` enforcement in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data` (the block that checked `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans:` and emitted `segment_span_count_exceeded` is deleted). Meanwhile, the Lua script `add-buffer.lua` introduces a hardcoded eviction cap of `1000` (`if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000) end`). This makes span-count limiting no longer tied to the Python-configured `self.max_segment_spans`, so any deployment with `max_segment_spans` set below 1000 would no longer have that stricter limit enforced (it will allow up to 1000).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:~140 — `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is read with no fallback; a message produced before this field was added to the schema (or with a null value) raises KeyError and fails the entire consumer batch (and `None` would also be rejected as a `zadd` score); should use `.get()` with a fallback such as `val["timestamp"]`.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py`, the diff adds a required `Span.end_timestamp_precise` field and populates it via `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` after `rapidjson.loads(payload.value)`. This is an unguarded dict key access; if any consumed message lacks that key (e.g., older producers / malformed payload), it will raise `KeyError` and abort batch processing. The diff provides no fallback/default and the new Redis `zadd` path in `buffer.py` also assumes a valid numeric score.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~819 — `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is documented as an 'Enhanced cursor-based paginator,' but it is a copy of the offset-based `OffsetPaginator` (pages by `cursor.offset` slicing, never by cursor value); the added cursors.py comment likewise claims negative offsets are 'allowed' when nothing supports them — the docs describe behavior the code does not have.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` does use `cursor.value` (via `cursor_value = self.value_from_cursor(cursor)` and `queryset = self.build_queryset(cursor_value, cursor.is_prev)`), so it is not “never by cursor value” nor simply a copy of an offset-only paginator. Also, the diff explicitly adds logic intended to allow negative offsets in both the generic slicing change (`start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset`) and in `OptimizedCursorPaginator` when `enable_advanced_features` is set, so the claim that “nothing supports them” is not grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:~70 — New undocumented `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter makes the same endpoint use a different paginator with different edge-case semantics depending on the caller's privileges (superuser/global-access vs. everyone else), an invisible, unversioned API behavior change that is also unrelated to this PR's stated purpose (spans buffer).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new query parameter `optimized_pagination` in `organization_auditlogs.py` (`use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) that conditionally switches the endpoint from `DateTimePaginator` to the newly added `OptimizedCursorPaginator` only for `request.user.is_superuser` or `organization_context.member.has_global_access`. This makes the same endpoint potentially return different pagination semantics depending on caller privileges and an unversioned query param, and it is indeed unrelated to the spans-buffer changes elsewhere in the PR. This is a concrete scope/API-contract concern visible in the diff, though not necessarily a functional defect when the param is not used.
